Reference guide to phone survey methods used at IPA—including CATI, IVR, and SMS surveys—covering implementation criteria, operational benefits and constraints, and links to tools, templates, and academic briefs. Keywords include: phone surveys, remote data collection, survey methodology, and data collection reference.

:::{.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Key Takeaways

- Survey modes (CATI, IVR, SMS) have distinct implementation considerations and trade-offs.
- Selection should be based on technical feasibility, research design, and respondent accessibility.
- IPA provides downloadable templates and synthesized research evidence to support deployment.
:::

## Introduction

Phone surveys are a core method of data collection at IPA, especially when in-person surveys are not feasible due to logistical, health, or cost constraints. They allow real-time data collection for monitoring and evaluation, are scalable across regions, and can adapt to diverse research designs. During the COVID-19 pandemic, IPA used phone surveys extensively to continue collecting high-quality data.

## Survey Modes

| Mode | Description | Requires Enumerator | Best For | Limitations |
|------|-------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| **CATI** | Live interviews conducted by enumerators using software | ✔️ | High data quality, complex questionnaires | Higher cost, training needed |
| **IVR** | Automated audio prompts with responses via keypad/voice | ❌ | Large samples, short surveys | Low engagement, drop-off risk |
| **SMS** | Text-based questionnaires sent via mobile | ❌ | Simple surveys, frequent updates | Literacy and character limits |
| **Web** | Online surveys accessed via links | ❌ | Literate, connected populations | Limited reach in LMICs |

## Implementation Considerations

### Technical Feasibility

- Access to valid and active phone numbers
- Consistent phone ownership or access among respondents
- Network coverage and device compatibility

### Resource Requirements

- Enumerator training (for CATI)
- Budget for airtime, incentives, or SMS credits
- Tools for remote tracking and call monitoring

### Research Design Compatibility

- Questionnaire complexity and length
- Ability to randomize or stratify sample
- Suitability of mode for the target population

## Operational Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Random Enumerator Assignment** | Allocation independent of location, promotes fairness |
| **Flexible Scheduling** | Calls can be made when respondents are more available |
| **Real-Time Monitoring** | Supervisors can audit live calls for quality control |
| **Validation Checks** | Built-in form logic reduces errors |
| **Tracking Systems** | Enables logging of call attempts, statuses, reschedules |

## Advantages and Challenges

### Advantages

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
- Lower operational costs
- Remote deployment at scale
- Real-time data entry and supervision
- No travel or field logistics required
- Useful for emergency response and sensitive data
:::

### Challenges

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
- Higher risk of attrition and refusals
- Limited ability to build rapport
- Risk of excluding low-access populations
- Language barriers may be harder to navigate
- Privacy concerns if others overhear calls
:::

## Summary: Best Practices Checklist

- ✅ Send pre-survey SMS or WhatsApp notifications
- ✅ Use CATI for complex or sensitive questionnaires
- ✅ Schedule calls during off-peak hours to improve pickup
- ✅ Use templates and plug-ins to reduce error and increase speed
- ✅ Track call attempts and outcomes to manage attrition
- ✅ Offer modest incentives where feasible
- ✅ Monitor for mode effects and adjust design if needed
